write.title: Write configuration
write.info:
NiCo writes the current configuration to your NixOS directory and creates a checkpoint – like a time machine for your config.

You can return to any earlier checkpoint in the admin panel if something goes wrong.
write.regenNote: The form-managed file is regenerated completely in the process. Your own comments and formatting outside of Nix bricks are not preserved – only content inside a Nix brick is safe.

validator.d.snapper_btrfs.unmounted: Snapper only works on mounted filesystems.
validator.d.snapper_btrfs.notbtrfs: Snapper only supports btrfs. The mountpoint has to be a btrfs subvolume.
validator.d.btrfs_without_btrfs.no_btrfs: The config builds and boots, but the maintenance jobs do nothing: scrub and balance exist only for btrfs. On ext4 or another file system, switch both off.
validator.d.btrfs_without_btrfs.root_not: The balance job NiCo generates works on / specifically. If the btrfs file system lives elsewhere, the job has no effect and fails on every run.
validator.d.btrfs_without_btrfs.other_ho: The check reads the mountpoints of the running system. Run the validator again on the machine in question.

validator.d.git_large_log:
Path: {0}
The file only holds rebuild output and can be deleted without a second thought. NiCo writes the log to {1} these days – this one is left over from an earlier version.
validator.d.hm_orphan_root: The file is not imported anywhere and most likely has no effect. It can be deleted.
validator.d.hm_user_defined: The files in {0}/ are not referenced from the flake. Add home-manager.users.<username> = import ./<file>.nix in flake.nix or in a module it includes.
validator.d.hm_allowunfree: allowUnfree is enabled in NiCo, but nixpkgs.config.allowUnfree = true is not set in {0}. Unfree packages in Home Manager are rejected without it.
validator.d.hm_state_version_match:
{0} line {1}: system.stateVersion = "{2}"
{3} line {4}: home.stateVersion = "{5}"
Both values have to be identical.
validator.d.brix_nested:
NiCo only manages the outer brick. The inner one does not appear in the brick list and is deleted along with the outer one when that is deleted or moved.
Nix itself does not care – the markers are comments.
To fix it: in the raw editor remove either the two outer or the two inner marker lines, not both pairs.
validator.d.brix_redundant: Options recognised in section {0}. After an import, check that all settings were carried over correctly.
validator.d.swap_in_snapshot:
Btrfs permanently refuses to snapshot a subvolume with an active swapfile. The config still builds and boots – the failure only shows up at the next timeline snapshot, after which btrfs-cleaner/btrfs-transaction can keep a core busy indefinitely.

What was checked is the state of the running system (/proc/swaps and findmnt), not the content of the config files. After a change, the result only counts once you have rebuilt and rebooted.

Fix: give the swap its own subvolume (outside the snapshotted hierarchy), add fileSystems."/swap" with subvol=swap, point swapDevices at /swap/swapfile, and create the swapfile anew with chattr +C (NoCOW) instead of moving it.
validator.d.swap_in_snapshot.other_host: The check reads the mountpoints of the running system. Run the validator again on the machine in question.
validator.d.host_checks_pending: Some rules read the running system (mountpoints, disks, architecture) and therefore only apply to "{0}". For the hosts listed, the validator has to run on that machine. NiCo remembers the result in config.json and shows it here on every machine once the config is in sync.

git.foreign.title: Foreign files found
git.foreign.body: These files are in the config directory but are not part of the NixOS config. Should they be included in git or excluded from it?
git.foreign.cleanupBody: These files are tracked in git but do not belong to the config. Removing takes them out of git (the file stays on disk, the git history is kept) and adds them to .gitignore. Keep remembers the file as intentional.
git.foreign.sectionHint: Files that do not belong to the config: NiCo asks before a checkpoint whether they should be included in git or excluded.

git.hygiene.title: Git hygiene
git.hygiene.body: This config has a few issues that let files end up in version control which do not belong there. Once taken in, they are hard to get rid of.
git.hygiene.gitignoreMissing: There is no .gitignore – NiCo files such as logs, backups and zips end up in version control without being asked for.
git.hygiene.oldLog: An old rebuild log ({0} MB) is still sitting in the config directory. NiCo keeps it elsewhere these days.
git.hygiene.oldLogTracked: An old rebuild log ({0} MB) is under version control. That is exactly what blocks every transfer to the server sooner or later.
git.hygiene.foreign: {0} files are under version control that do not belong to the config.
git.hygiene.large: {0} file(s) are too large for version control.
git.hygiene.largePublished: {0} oversized file(s) are already on the server and can no longer be removed safely.
git.large.title: Oversized files
git.large.body: Files larger than {0} MB do not belong in version control: they block the transfer to the server and can only be removed later with considerable effort. What is possible here depends on where the file sits.
git.large.publishedNote: These files are already on the server. They could only be removed by rewriting the published history – which makes the copies on your other machines unusable. NiCo deliberately does not offer that.
git.large.deleteFromDisk: Delete the files from disk as well
git.large.backupNote: The previous state is kept in full in the backup branch {0}. Nothing is lost while it exists – but the disk space is only freed once it is removed.
git.large.dropBackup: Remove the backup and free the space
git.skippedLarge.title: Oversized file not included
git.skippedLarge.body: This file is too large for version control and was not included in the snapshot. It stays on disk unchanged. The reason: files like this permanently block every transfer to the server and are hard to remove from the history afterwards.
git.pushNothing: Nothing to transfer – the server is at the same state.
git.pullNothing: Nothing new – you are already up to date.
git.pushErr.AUTH_FAILED: Authentication failed. Wrong username or password (token).
git.pushErr.FILE_TOO_LARGE: An oversized file is stuck in the git history. The server refuses it, and pushing again will not change that – the file has to be removed from the history.
git.pushErr.TIMEOUT: Timeout – the operation was cancelled before it finished. That does not necessarily mean something is broken: with a lot of data to transfer or a slow connection it can simply take too long.
git.pushErr.NOT_FAST_FORWARD: Push rejected – pull first, resolve conflicts, then try again.
git.pushErr.NOT_FOUND: Repository not found. Check the URL or access rights may be missing.
git.pushErr.NO_KEY: SSH key missing or not authorized. No SSH key is set up for this repository on this machine.
git.pushErr.NO_NETWORK: Network error. Could not connect to the server.
git.pushErr.NO_WRITE: No write access to the repository. The account used has no push permission.
